questions.question: A student writes the LP: maximize $5x_1+4x_2$ subject to $6x_1+4x_2\le24$, $x_1+2x_2\le6$ and $x_1,x_2\ge0$, but never says what $x_1$ and $x_2$ represent. What is the consequence of this omission?
options: The LP cannot be solved until the variables are described in words.
Nothing is lost, as the coefficients already reveal what each variable is.
The LP can be solved, but its solution cannot be read as decisions.
Only the units are lost; the meanings follow from the objective.

questions.question: An investor formulates an LP to split a budget of 10000 euros between a bond fund and a stock fund, with expected annual returns of 3% and 7% and at most 6000 euros in stocks. Which quantity is a decision variable of this LP?
options: The number of euros to be placed in the stock fund
The expected annual return of 7% on the stock fund
The total budget of 10000 euros to be invested
The largest expected return the investor can reach

questions.question: A chemical plant asks for a linear program to plan its weekly output $x_1$ and $x_2$, in tonnes, of two fertilizers, which can be produced in any nonnegative amount. Should the restrictions $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{Z}$ be added?
options: Yes; every production quantity in a model must be a whole number.
No; tonnes are divisible, so the requested LP keeps them continuous.
Yes; LP optima are integers anyway, so the restriction is harmless.
No; integer restrictions would make the constraints nonlinear.

questions.question: In a model with nonnegative decision variables $x_1,x_2$ and $x_1+x_2>0$, which requirement cannot be written as a linear constraint, even after rearranging?

A furniture maker formulates an LP for weekly production, with profit per unit of each product as objective coefficients. A monthly rent of 5000 euros is paid whatever is produced. How should the rent affect these per-unit coefficients?
options: Rent divided by planned output should be subtracted from each coefficient.
The full rent should be subtracted from each unit profit, as all costs count.
It should become a decision variable, so the model can try to reduce it.
Not at all; it is the same for every plan, so the best plan is unchanged.

questions.question: A workshop sells a lamp for 45 euros. Each lamp uses 12 euros of material and 1.5 hours of labour paid at 14 euros per hour. With $x$ the number of lamps made per week, what is the profit coefficient of $x$ in the LP objective?
options: 19 euros per lamp
12 euros per lamp
33 euros per lamp
31.5 euros per lamp

questions.question: A bakery bakes $x_W$ trays of white bread and $x_R$ trays of rye bread per day, and it must bake at least twice as many white trays as rye trays. Which constraint expresses this requirement?
options: $2x_W\ge x_R$
$x_W\le2x_R$
$x_W-x_R\ge2$
$x_W\ge2x_R$

questions.question: Each unit of product 1 needs 30 minutes on a press and each unit of product 2 needs 45 minutes; the press is available 20 hours per week. With $x_1,x_2$ the weekly units made, which constraint correctly expresses the press capacity?
A firm produces $x_1$ and $x_2$ tonnes of two products, with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. At least 40% of total output must be product 1. Which linear constraint expresses this requirement?

A table needs 4 hours of carpentry and 2 hours of finishing; a chair needs 3 hours of carpentry and 1 hour of finishing. Each week 120 carpentry hours and 50 finishing hours are available. With $x_T$ tables and $x_C$ chairs made per week, which constraints describe the labour limits?
options: $4x_T+2x_C\le120$ and $3x_T+x_C\le50$
$4x_T+3x_C\ge120$ and $2x_T+x_C\ge50$
$4x_T+3x_C\le120$ and $2x_T+x_C\le50$
$6x_T+4x_C\le170$ for all labour together

questions.question: A planning LP has $x$ = units produced next month and $d$ = change in the number of workers from this month to next (positive for hiring, negative for layoffs; both are allowed). Which sign restrictions belong in the formulation?
options: $x\ge0$, while $d$ stays free in sign as layoffs are allowed
$x\ge0$ and $d\ge0$, as LP variables must be nonnegative
None for either, since the constraints settle the signs
$d\ge0$ only, as output is never negative at an optimum

questions.question: A warehouse can hold at most 500 pallets. A modeller writes $x_1+x_2=500$ for the numbers of pallets of two goods stored, instead of $x_1+x_2\le500$. What does this change in the model?
options: It forces a full warehouse and excludes plans that leave space unused.
Nothing, because an optimal plan always fills all the available space.
It relaxes the model, because an equality is easier to satisfy.
It replaces the capacity limit by a minimum stock of 500 pallets.

questions.question: A firm makes products A and B at two plants, each with its own weekly limit on machine hours, and either product can be made at either plant. A modeller defines only $x_A$ and $x_B$, the total units of A and B made per week. Is this choice of variables adequate for the formulation?
options: Yes: the two plants' hour limits can be added into a single constraint on total hours.
No: each plant's hours depend on where units are made, so product-plant variables are needed.
Yes: plant capacities are parameters, so they need no decision variables of their own.
Yes, provided the demand for each product is written as its own constraint on $x_A$ and $x_B$.

questions.question: An LP maximizes $3x_1+x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\le4$ and $x_1\ge0$. Here $x_2$ counts units of a product and was meant to be nonnegative, but $x_2\ge0$ was left out. What does this LP, as written, give?
options: Optimum 12 at $(4,0)$, the best plan once $x_2\ge0$ is in place
Optimum 4 at $(0,4)$, the only point where two boundaries meet
No finite optimum: $x_1=4+t$, $x_2=-t$ gives $12+2t$ for every $t\ge0$
No solution, because a variable without a sign restriction is undefined

questions.question: A machine makes product P at a rate of 4 units per hour, and each unit of P earns a profit of 5 euros. A modeller defines $h$ = machine hours per week spent on P. Which objective coefficient of $h$ gives the weekly profit from P?
options: 20 euros per hour
5 euros per hour
1.25 euros per hour
4 euros per hour

questions.question: In an LP, $x_A$ and $x_B$ are the amounts of paints A and B made per day in hundreds of litres, and $z$ is daily profit in euros. The optimal solution is $(x_A,x_B)=(2.5,4)$ with optimal value 380. What does this mean in practice?
options: Make 2.5 litres of A and 4 litres of B per day, for a profit of 380 euros.
Make 200 litres of A and 400 litres of B, since output comes in whole hundreds.
Make 250 litres of A and 400 litres of B per day, for a profit of 380 euros.
Make 250 litres of A and 400 litres of B per day, earning 380 euros per litre.

questions.question: For nonnegative amounts $x_1,x_2$ (tonnes of two ingredients in a blend), a share requirement reads $\frac{x_1}{x_1+x_2}\le\frac{1}{3}$. Why may an LP use $x_1\le\frac{x_1+x_2}{3}$ instead?
options: Any inequality may be multiplied through by an expression in the variables.
Ratios of variables are linear, so the change only simplifies the notation.
It may not, since the linear version allows shares above one third.
For any actual blend $x_1+x_2>0$, so multiplying by it keeps the direction.

questions.question: In a production LP with constraint $2x_1+3x_2\le H$, the number $H$ of labour hours is usually a parameter. In which situation is it correct to make $H$ a decision variable instead?
options: When extra hours can be bought at a cost per hour in the objective, up to a limit.
When next month's available hours are uncertain, so their value is only an estimate.
Whenever $H$ stands on the right-hand side of a constraint, as right-hand sides are chosen.
Whenever the model should pick the best $H$, with no cost or limit attached to it.

questions.question: A requirement says that product 1 may be at most one third of total output $x_1+x_2$, with $x_1,x_2\ge0$. A colleague writes $x_1\le\frac{x_2}{3}$. For plans with positive total output, what largest share of total output does this constraint allow product 1?
options: One third, since the same fraction $\frac{1}{3}$ appears in it
One quarter, since $3x_1\le x_2$ means $4x_1\le x_1+x_2$
Three quarters, since $x_2$ may be three times $x_1$
No fixed share, since it only compares $x_1$ with $x_2$

questions.question: Each rented truck carries at most 20 tonnes and costs 300 euros; 130 tonnes must be moved. The LP minimize $300y$ subject to $20y\ge130$, $y\ge0$, where $y$ is the number of trucks, gives $y=6.5$. What is the cheapest plan with whole trucks?
options: 6 trucks for 1800 euros; rounding the LP answer down is safe
7 trucks for 2100 euros, as whole trucks need integrality
6.5 trucks for 1950 euros; LP fractions are valid answers
7 trucks for 1950 euros; the LP cost already is the true cost
